title: Uniqueness of Hermite coefficients
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\gamma_n$ be the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belong to $L^2(\gamma_n)$. If a family of real coefficients $(c_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}$ has its Hermite series converge in $L^2(\gamma_n)$ to $f$, then for every $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, $c_\alpha=\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)H_\alpha(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)$, where $H_\alpha$ is the multivariate Hermite function indexed by $\alpha$.
hypotheses_covered: The dimension $n$ is a natural number, with no further restriction.
The function $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belongs to $L^2$ for the product standard Gaussian measure.
The coefficient family indexed by $\mathbb N^n$ has its Hermite series converge in $L^2$ to the equivalence class of $f$.
